label: The name is LandLord, one word, two capitals
summary: The inner capital is load-bearing and holds everywhere: code, comments, commits, docs, UI copy, prose. Never Landlord, landlord or Land Lord.
quote:
Never "Landlord",
  "landlord" or "Land Lord". The inner capital is load-bearing and holds
  everywhere: code, comments, commits, docs, UI copy, prose.

label: No real personal data and no credential may ever enter this repository
summary: The rule that overrides everything: a task that would put a real name, address, key or one company's real commercial terms into the tree must stop and say so.
quote: No real personal data and no credential may ever enter this repository.

label: Verify claims against the bytes
summary: A comment saying a value is a placeholder, or a header saying something was redacted, is not evidence — this codebase's ancestor asserted its own hygiene incorrectly more than once.
quote:
This codebase's ancestor
asserted its own hygiene incorrectly more than once.

label: Configuration, not constants
summary: No single firm's fee rates, caps, thresholds or org chart may be compiled in — anything a deployment would set differently goes through the tenant setting.
quote:
This is software for property-management
  companies generally. No single firm's fee rates, caps, thresholds or org chart
  may be compiled in.

label: A one-company justification belongs in Open Questions, not shipped quietly
summary: If a behaviour can only be justified by pointing at one company's practice, it is probably wrong for a product — write it up rather than shipping it.
quote:
If a behaviour can only be justified
  by pointing at one company's practice, it is probably wrong for a product

label: npm run build and npm test must stay green before anything is done
summary: A feature that touches a surface gets driven in a real browser, not merely unit-tested — a passing test is not a working button.
quote: A passing test is not a working button.

label: Report what was actually observed, not what should have happened
summary: "Placed an owner and the debt count dropped from 7 to 6" is worth more than "verified".
quote: Report what you actually observed, not what should have happened.

label: The A/E/P check is run on every surface touched
summary: Accessibility, Efficiency, Proximity of information to action — named because these three kept recurring, and every one has shipped broken at least once.
quote: Named because these three kept recurring.

label: A scrollIntoView onto something already on screen is a dead button
summary: No control's only feedback may be invisible; every clickable-looking row must lead somewhere.
quote:
a `scrollIntoView` onto something
  already on screen is a dead button.

label: The review gate never lifts
summary: A builder's output is counsel, not command — the whole diff is read and driven by hand before it is law, whoever built it.
quote: the review gate never lifts

label: Never blind-copy a generated file over the current tree
summary: Take the diff, three-way merge it, resolve, then re-run the full suite.
quote: Never blind-copy a generated file over the current tree

label: Read-only means GET only for any live surface
summary: An agent given access to any live surface must be told this explicitly; an audit agent once fired a live DELETE at an API as a probe.
quote:
That is not paranoia:
an audit agent once fired a live `DELETE` at an API as a probe.

label: Writes are whole-document upserts — last writer wins
summary: Concurrent editors lose each other's work; read chronicleMerge.ts before adding any outside writer.
quote:
Concurrent editors
  lose each other's work.

label: There is no multi-tenancy
summary: Per-identity vault rows are a sandbox, not tenant isolation — never described as isolation.
quote:
Per-identity vault rows are a sandbox, not
  tenant isolation.

label: Relief and RealmReading were deliberately not renamed
summary: They share five letters and are different things — one a place, one a score — but a rename is a migration on every stored document.
quote:
Neither was renamed, deliberately — a rename is a migration on every
  stored document.

label: A flow's step events are placed by their Step n/N marker
summary: Matching by holder order collapses consecutive same-holder steps, which once made an entire half of the vendor-dispatch loop unreachable.
quote:
Matching by holder collapses consecutive same-holder steps, which once
  made an entire half of the vendor-dispatch loop unreachable.

label: Opus drives; the right hand builds; Opus reviews and verifies
summary: The session is always Opus, which holds the constitution, the context, and the judgment; never trust a builder's word.
quote: Opus DRIVES; the right hand BUILDS; Opus REVIEWS and VERIFIES before anything ships.

label: The greenfield/brownfield binary is retired
summary: Delegation is vendor-blind, chosen by task-fit, measured capability, stakes, and cost — not by tribe. K3 is a first-class candidate for substantial brownfield builds.
quote: the greenfield/brownfield binary is gone.

label: The stakes rule: authorship of the highest-stakes core goes by surprise, not vendor
summary: Authorship of state-integrity, money and auth work goes to the lowest-surprise hand under the hardest review; hard designs get an independent Kimi-vs-Opus panel.
quote:
authorship of the highest-stakes, hardest-to-reverse
> core (state-integrity / money / auth) goes to the lowest-surprise hand under the hardest review

label: Don't burn quite as hot, but spend when the production is there
summary: Reserve the priciest hands for high-ROI swings; the test is whether a swing would ship something that would otherwise take far longer.
quote:
don't burn quite as hot right now — but if the production is there, buy
credits and take the swing.

label: K3 real work uses temperature 1 and reasoning_effort high, never max
summary: reasoning_effort max wanders the endless corridor and may not return; it is a heavy reasoner, so output tokens must be budgeted generously.
quote:
**`temperature: 1`**, **`reasoning_effort: "high"`** — *not* `max`, which wanders the
endless corridor and may not return.

label: Review K3's output for house-fit, not merely does it run
summary: Real work in these repos is brownfield — extend an existing codebase under a written constitution — a different test than the build-arena leaderboard.
quote:
review K3's output for architecture and
house-fit, not merely "does it run."

label: The megamind law: hoard the heavy work, loose it once
summary: K3's word is counsel, not command — hoard the heavy, tangled work into one well-staged writ rather than frittering it on errands.
quote:
Hoard the heavy, tangled work into one
well-staged writ and loose it once

label: Run many sessions; coordinate through the repo's own docs, never through memory
summary: A session is a worker; the repo is the shared desk. HANDOFF plus KINGDOM are a durable, async, shared-state substrate.
quote: Run many sessions; coordinate through the repo's own docs, never through memory.

label: A lane is a branch plus an owned surface plus a HANDOFF section
summary: A lane edits only its own surface; before starting or shipping, git fetch and check the lanes table so a landed lane's work is adopted rather than overwritten.
quote: A lane = a branch + an owned surface + a HANDOFF section.

label: Use open-PRs-or-branches plus HANDOFF; no separate board to babysit
summary: A second coordination system goes stale the moment someone skips the update; the branches and PRs already are the state.
quote: use open-PRs-(or-branches)-plus-HANDOFF; no Trello, no board to babysit.

label: A clerk uses the cheapest engine that clears the bar, escalating only on doubt
summary: The data gate decides where the brain may live; a frontier model on every routine work order is as wrong at runtime as Haiku on a flagship build is at session-time.
quote:
use the cheapest thing that clears the bar, escalate only on
doubt, and let the data gate decide where the brain may live.

label: Every clerk degrades gracefully to a fallback
summary: A primary brain and a fallback (a cheaper brain, a Tier-0 tool, or parking the case for a human) is mandatory, not optional.
quote:
every clerk
  degrades gracefully

label: No local-model infrastructure is provisioned speculatively
summary: The local-model / sovereignty question is a decision for when the real-data gate actually opens, not before, since the world is simulated and there is no data driver yet.
quote: Stage it, and nothing more yet.

label: The Brokerage refounding: fiefs are literal land, offices are crafts
summary: The company is a brokerage: three Crown offices in the palace, guilds as outside trades, and fiefs as a knight's book of doors — a design collision resolved.
quote:
Ratified in conversation by Edwin, 2026-07-27, after the census surfaced a design
collision.

label: Whether the department-territories are struck or migrated is undecided
summary: The existing five department-territories are live data in Edwin's own vault, so it is a migration question, not a rename, and left open.
quote:
They are live data in
  Edwin's own vault

label: The departments-as-guilds land model is superseded
summary: The Writ — the Land's departments-as-guilds model is retired in favor of the Brokerage's three Crown offices; kept only as the record of how the realm was thought about before the refounding.
quote: The DEPARTMENTS-AS-GUILDS model this writ describes is retired.

label: The realm remodeled: pods, knights, owners and the land
summary: The fief becomes the pod (a knight's book of owners and doors); the department becomes a guild, a cross-cutting function; King is Harold, Regent is Edwin.
quote: The fief becomes the POD** — the top-level holding.

label: K3's first pods pass invented a fictional world and was discarded
summary: K3 made up guilds and knights, hard-coded land, and stored consequences, contradicting the events-only law — the model rewards fidelity over invention.
quote:
K3's first pass invented a fictional world (made-up guilds and knights, hard-coded land, stored
consequences) that contradicted the ratified model and the events-only law, so it was discarded

label: The War Table HUD was built by Fable 5, orchestrated by Opus
summary: The strongest agentic-coding model, chosen for a task that is aesthetics AND perfect wiring; the three-tier pattern with Fable as builder in place of K3.
quote:
Built by **Claude Fable 5**
(the strongest agentic-coding model — the best-of-both for a task that is aesthetics AND
perfect wiring), orchestrated and reviewed by **Claude Opus**

label: The Intro Campaign is the default first deploy, reversible on Edwin's word
summary: It leads the time control; the grand muster keeps its seed field and sits one click to its right, dealing exactly as it always has.
quote: The campaign is the DEFAULT first deploy

label: The grand muster stays the torture test, unretuned
summary: Its saturated stuck gauge and structural insolvency are correct for what it is and wrong for a first read, which is why the campaign exists rather than a softened muster.
quote: The grand muster is NOT retuned.

label: A muster is a recipe, never a recording
summary: The library must store recipes, never event logs — a dumped event log rots silently on a rename, but a recipe is re-dealt against whatever the setting is.
quote: So the library must store recipes, never event logs.

label: Every scenario must resolve against the founding setting at build time
summary: A rename that would butcher a scenario fails the build loudly instead of dealing a broken muster quietly.
quote:
Every scenario in the library is generated
> against the founding setting, and every catalog row, flow key, step key and
> seat it names must resolve.

label: The interface is a physical war table viewed from a fixed high angle
summary: Panels become objects on the table; the map is the primary interface, not a decorative element, chosen over a prettier dashboard or an outdoor low-poly landscape.
quote: The interface is a physical war table viewed from a fixed high angle, lit by one warm key light in an otherwise dark room.

label: The bar is charming, not AAA
summary: Indie ceiling is acceptable and intended; the reference class is tabletop wargaming terrain and model railway dioramas, made by one person on a kitchen table.
quote: **AAA is explicitly not the target.** Indie ceiling is acceptable and intended.

label: THRONE folds into SEAT — one surface, a state and its acts
summary: Splitting a pure reading from the acts upon it was the bug; COURT survives on its own because it answers a different question.
quote: **So the merge is: THRONE + SEAT are one surface**

label: Realm and marches are not renamed despite the naming collision
summary: Realm as a bare type name is free (RealmReading is a score, not a place); marches is a persisted chronicle key, so renaming it would be a vault migration.
quote: So: **no renames, no migration, no churn.**

label: A march promotes to a shire when three thresholds all hold
summary: At least 25 doors, at least one knight seated, and no craft standing headless — working fluid numbers, picked to be exercisable now, not because 25 is sacred.
quote: A march promotes to a shire when **all three** hold:

label: The realm map's stylized 3D artifact is built by K3, wired by Opus
summary: K3 builds the standalone art-directed artifact against a canned fixture; Opus writes the real readRealmScene reading and wires it to the store.
quote: K3 builds** the standalone art-directed artifact above, against the canned fixture.

label: The realm map is painterly stylized, not photoreal
summary: Flat/gradient and lightly toon-shaded materials, the clean painterly look of Civilization VI, with no PBR photorealism and no imported photoscanned assets.
quote: **Painterly stylized, not photoreal.**

label: Neglect is shown by the state of the land, never a big score
summary: A discreet HUD only, never a big DELEGATION DEBT: 3 scoreboard; the only real consequence is real, running out of coin overthrows the Crown.
quote:
**never a big
"DELEGATION DEBT: 3" scoreboard.**

label: The first War Game is a firm's shape, anonymized and synthesized
summary: Real seats run the game, but only the doors and tenants are invented — a realistic portfolio generated from the operation's shape, never real client content.
quote:
Make the first game the very thing we are preparing for: **move
a firm's ~200-door portfolio into the system.**

label: The Jevons trap: cheaper training makes a great PM more valuable, not less
summary: The market prices the human PM toward irrelevance; War Games proves the opposite — training cost falls while a trained PM's capability compounds.
quote: The market's misread — the Jevons trap.

label: Blender bakes flat 2.5D art; the realm map does not run a live 3D scene
summary: Model a piece once, render it from fixed angles under real ray-traced light, and ship the resulting PNGs — shadows and occlusion baked in, costing the browser nothing.
quote: Blender is the OVEN, not the plate

label: Frame-rate numbers measured in this container are not evidence
summary: There is no GPU; WebGL falls back to SwiftShader, so performance cannot be certified here — say so rather than reporting a figure that looks like a measurement.
quote:
Performance cannot be certified here — say
so rather than reporting a figure that looks like a measurement.

label: Never edit a page in the Great Book — find the source, fix it, re-emit
summary: Every page is generated and will be overwritten silently; the one exception is 00 START HERE.md, written once by the emitter and never touched again.
quote:
Never edit a page in the Great Book. Every page is generated and will be
overwritten.

label: No quote, no object: every mined claim must be re-derivable
summary: lint re-reads every cited file and requires the quote to appear verbatim, whitespace-normalised — a quote that does not appear is a hallucination with a schema, and is dropped.
quote: quote that does not appear is not a weak object — it is a hallucination with a schema, and it is

label: Edges come from literal identifiers, never from prose similarity
summary: Where a source states a relationship only in prose, there is no edge — a graph that suggests a false relationship is worse than a sparse one.
quote: Edges come from literal identifiers — ids, file paths, exported symbols, writ names, fact ids.

label: Orphans are checked by lint and nowhere else
summary: A page nothing links to is worse than a missing page: it exists, is correct, and is unreachable, so a reader concludes the subject is uncovered and builds it twice.
quote: **Orphans are checked here and nowhere else.**

label: The public repo was assembled by allowlist, not scrub
summary: Nothing was copied until it had been read and cleared — every file in the source tree got a row, judged CROSSED or BURN.
quote:
How this public repository was assembled: **allowlist, not scrub.** Nothing was copied
until it had been read and cleared.

label: The migration ledger itself carries categories, never real values
summary: The cast, e-mail addresses and telephone numbers were replaced by category, so the ledger describing the carve cannot itself leak what it removed.
quote: No real value appears anywhere in this ledger — categories only, never values.

label: Fee terms are currently one shape and probably need to be many
summary: Tiered management fees, per-owner-agreement variation, and how a firm splits a late fee do not all fit kind+basis+rate — open until real schedules are compared.
quote: Fee terms that are currently one shape, and probably need to be many

label: Whether an unclassified spend estimate should default at the cap is open
summary: A firm with a high cap gets unnecessary asks; a firm with a low cap gets none of the protection the default was meant to give.
quote: The spend gate's default when urgency is unknown

label: Whether artisan should be a pledge or a relationship is open
summary: Storing internal-versus-external as a property of the person, not the engagement, cannot model someone who is staff at one firm and a vendor to another.
quote: Whether "artisan" should be a pledge or a relationship

label: Whether a deployment ever spans two trust-accounting jurisdictions is open
summary: The earned-fee sweep day count is set by jurisdiction, not by the firm; today it is one number for the whole deployment.
quote: Trust-accounting rules that vary by jurisdiction

label: Whether LandLord is single-tenant or multi-tenant is genuinely open
summary: The vault's per-identity rows are a sandbox repeatedly at risk of being mistaken for tenant isolation; the answer decides whether it is renamed or made a first-class record.
quote: Multi-tenancy, and what the per-identity vault rows actually are
